title: Graph-Transformer-based Surrogate Model for Accelerated Converter Circuit Topology Design
problem: Automated analog circuit topology design faces combinatorial explosion of the topology space and time-consuming circuit evaluation. Data discontinuity in topology space makes accurate performance prediction for unseen topologies exceptionally difficult.
motivation: Accelerating circuit topology design enables faster exploration of design space compared to traditional manual design and high-fidelity simulation.
method: The GTN model embeds voltage changes in circuit loops and current flows in connected devices using graph representations. A graph-transformer architecture processes these embeddings to predict circuit performance without expensive simulation. The approach enables accurate predictions for circuits with previously unseen topologies.
key_novelty: Using Graph-Transformer Networks with voltage and current flow embeddings to enable accurate performance prediction of unseen circuit topologies.
contributions: Graph-Transformer Network (GTN) surrogate model achieving less than 5% relative error with 196× speedup versus high-fidelity simulation
Novel circuit embedding scheme capturing voltage changes in loops and current flows for topology representation
Automatic design framework discovering circuits of comparable quality to simulation-based design in up to 98.2% less time
Empirical validation on power converter circuit design outperforming analytical approaches and baseline GNN methods

metrics.other: 98.2% time reduction in automatic design framework

primary_theme: Learning-based circuit topology optimization via surrogate models
